## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6edd9b16bede619bacb8800693bfa3e5d6316300`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read, and nothing else: card objectui#12191 (body and all seven comments: triage 6120144083, re-grade 6121311525, ruling 6121792024 letter A+, claim 6122111640, os-dev-report 6122743522, ACCEPT 6122779145, ACCEPT amendment 6122901344); PR #12230 (body, file list of 8 files at +593/-26, the net diff against `main` at the head); the check-runs on the head; `packages/core/package.json` and `packages/core/src/index.ts` at the head for the published reach; objectstack-ai/objectstack#23010 for the spec half's wording. Read-only: no worktree, build, test or gate run.

Check-runs on the head, as read for this record: 43 runs, 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` by design (two coverage jobs and dependabot), 0 `failure`, 0 `in_progress`. Among the successes: Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Claim Re-read, Type Check, Lint, Build & E2E, Test shards 1 to 8, Test (dist pins), README Export Check, Bundle Analysis, Governed Surface Queue Guard.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface, `@object-ui/core`, widened — RIGHT.** `classifyNavigationTarget(url)` and `type NavigationTargetKind = 'web' | 'mail' | 'path'` are defined in the new `src/actions/navigationTarget.ts`, re-exported by `actions/index.ts`, which `src/index.ts` re-exports, which `exports["."]` reaches (`dist/index.js`, `dist/index.d.ts`). The ruling's "one symbol, two callers" crosses the core to app-shell package boundary, and app-shell depends on `@object-ui/core` (`workspace:*`), so the symbol has to be addressable from core's entry. The addition is declared in the changeset and the PR body.
2. **No public removal — RIGHT.** `ActionRunner.isValidUrl` was a `private` method, never callable from the `.d.ts`. `NAVIGATION_TARGET_REFUSAL` is a module constant, not exported.
3. **Runtime accept set of the runner (`type: 'url'`, its `navigation` alias, `onSuccess.navigate`):**
   - `mailto:` admitted and navigated IN PLACE through `window.location.href`; `openIn` not read; the host handler not called; `window.open` not called — RIGHT, as ruled. Pinned on the `url` door, the `navigation` alias with a flat `to`, the legacy `navigate.newTab: true`, `onSuccess.navigate` with `openIn: 'newTab'`, the no-handler case, and through a real `element:button` in the components pin.
   - `tel:` refused — RIGHT, as ruled (zero measured pull; one maintainer word adds it). The refusal text does not name `tel:`, and a pin asserts that.
   - `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `ftp:` and every other scheme refused — RIGHT.
   - Protocol-relative `//host` refused — RIGHT, and it is a NARROWING of the runner's runtime accept set: the old `startsWith('/')` admitted it and handed it to the host handler as `external: false`. The ruling lists `//evil.example/x` among the refused targets; the dev flagged the behaviour change; the changeset body states the from and to. The classifier also refuses `/` followed by a backslash and any target holding a tab, line feed or carriage return, the two spellings a browser's URL parser reads as `//host`: stricter than the ruling's letter, in the ruling's direction, pinned. RIGHT.
   - Upper-case `HTTP://`, `HTTPS://`, `MAILTO:` admitted — a widening the ruling did not spell. Scheme names are case-insensitive in the URL parser, objectstack-ai/objectstack#23010's spec text says case-insensitive, and the CTA's http test already was; one shared answer had to pick one rule. RIGHT, declared in the changeset.
   - The scheme form without slashes (`http:example.com`) stays refused — unchanged from before this PR, so not this diff's doing. It is a seam to watch: #23010's current wording admits any target whose scheme is `http:`, `https:` or `mailto:` by a scheme regex, so a bare `http:host` would pass that door and be refused here. Escalated under ③.
   - The refusal is one module constant naming `http://`, `https://`, `mailto:`, `/path` and `./path`, keeping the "Invalid URL" opening the existing refusal pins assert, and the `onSuccess.navigate` warning carries the same sentence. No i18n key moved. RIGHT.
4. **`resolveCtaHref` in `@object-ui/app-shell` — RIGHT.** Not reachable by name from app-shell's `exports["."]` entry (`src/index.ts` does not export it; the dialog is reached transitively through the console shell). Its three answers are unchanged: `web` as-is in a new tab, `mail` as-is in place, everything else control-plane-relative. New: `MAILTO:` passes as-is, where it used to be prefixed; declared. Its refused branch is unchanged, and this record notes one overstatement: the pin titled "never passes the refused target as-is" proves it only with a non-empty base; with an empty `apiBase`, `resolveCtaHref('javascript:alert(1)', '')` answers an href byte-identical to the input, exactly as the PR's H2 and acceptance notes say. Pre-existing, not widened by this diff.
5. **`isExternal` after the `/api/` promotion — RIGHT.** `Boolean(source.external) || classifyNavigationTarget(url) === 'web'` on the promoted URL answers what the old `startsWith('http://') || startsWith('https://')` answered, with the `source.external` override kept. The `isApiCall` full-page branch is unchanged.
6. **The single-definition pin — RIGHT.** It walks every non-test source under `packages/*/src` (population above 500, and it must contain both callers), asserts exactly one definer, the dialog's import from `@object-ui/core`, the runner's import from `./navigationTarget.js`, no scheme test in either file with comments masked, and a CONTROL that the scheme-test pattern finds the definition it guards. That is the ruling's "a pin asserts the single definition".
7. **Fork clause — RIGHT.** The callers are `navigateTo` (from `executeUrl`, `executeNavigation`, and the html-tier anchor's internal-link click), `navigateOnSuccess`, and the CTA anchor's `href`. All are user-click navigations; none is an iframe `src`, a fetch target or a server-side redirect. The set was not widened to fit a producer.
8. **Other URL readers untouched — RIGHT.** `sanitizeHref`, `UrlField` and `resolveNotificationTarget` are read and reported, not changed, as the claim's ⛔ required.
9. **Governed surfaces — none touched.** `.changeset/` and `packages/**` only; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`. This record is owed by the `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/12191-runner-admits-mailto.md` declares `@object-ui/core: minor` and `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. Core adds two names to its published entry, so `minor` is the floor a widening takes. Objectui never declares `major` (the fixed group follows objectstack's major; breaking semantics go into the body), and the body carries the breaking sentence: `//host` is now refused where the runner used to hand it to the navigation handler as an in-app path. RIGHT.
- App-shell adds no export and changes one component's internal answer: `patch`. RIGHT. `@object-ui/components` gains only a test file and is versioned with the fixed group regardless. RIGHT.
- No `skip-changeset`; Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check and Changeset Claim Re-read are all `success` on the head. The changeset body carries no model identifier.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stands at a line start on the PR body's second line, a legal spelling, and it matches the diff: the public surface widens by two names and the runtime accept set widens by `mailto:` and the upper-case schemes. The ruling set `no` for the objectui half ("no published schema; a runtime accept set") and left the lane free to read otherwise; the lane re-read it on the exports map, and this record agrees: the published surface is what the `exports` map reaches. The `//host` narrowing is a runtime accept set, which the ruling placed outside the declaration's domain, so the `(narrowing)` arm is not owed; objectui carries no ADR-0087 registry for the arm to steer. The claim comment's `Clause-②: no` is superseded by the ACCEPT amendment, which says so in writing.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6122743522, `deviations`:
1. Narrowed local verification (whole core suite plus every test reading an edited file; whole app-shell and components suites left to CI) — ANSWERED: Test shards 1 to 8 and Test (dist pins) are `success` on this head; the declared narrowing is closed by the check-runs.
2. The `element:button` pin is a new test file in `packages/components` with no components bump — ANSWERED, right: test-only, and the fixed group versions components with the family anyway.
3. `//host`, the backslash spelling and the control-character spellings refused — ANSWERED, right (① item 3): stricter in the ruling's direction, pinned, declared.
4. Upper-case schemes admitted — ANSWERED, right (① item 3): consistent with the spec half's case-insensitive rule, declared.
5. Model-free commit trailers — ANSWERED: the three commits on the PR end with the `Claude-Session` and `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair and no model identifier; the PR body and the changeset carry none. The repo rule wins over the harness reminder, as the dev read it.
6. One unlocked type-check run with an uncaptured exit — ANSWERED: superseded by the locked run at the head and by `Type Check` `success` on the head.

`open_questions`: none declared, none found.

`out_of_scope_findings`:
1. `resolveCtaHref`'s refused branch — ANSWERED: stands as recorded in the ACCEPT, with the one correction in ① item 4 (the pin's title overstates; the empty-base case is the disclosed one). Pre-existing, not widened. A card is owed the day a producer of a non-http(s), non-path CTA URL is named; none is today. Not a FAIL reason.
2. `executeActionSchema` copies `action.redirect` into `result.redirect` unchecked — ANSWERED: dormant; the only in-tree reader is the anchor tier for `type: 'url'`, which passes through `navigateTo`. Stands as recorded.
3. The H6 divergences (`sanitizeHref` admits `tel:`, `UrlField` links case-sensitive http(s) only, `resolveNotificationTarget` treats any scheme as external) — ANSWERED: outside the claim's file surface by its own ⛔; the contract's one scheme set is written in the spec half, and any reader that is to follow it is a card of its own.

Reviewer's escalation, one, to the spec half: objectstack-ai/objectstack#23010's door text admits the scheme form `http:host` without `//`, while the runner's `web` kind requires `://`. The spec seat should require the slashes for the two web schemes so the authoring door and the runner answer the same for that spelling; otherwise the trap this card closes re-opens on it. Not a FAIL on this PR: the runner's answer for that spelling is unchanged.
